search.snippet: What Is Happening To The Oldschool Runescape Economy? How Raids 4 Is Crashing The Economy (OSRS) No Help 44.8K subscribers Subscribe Jun 19, 2026 · What Is Happening To The Oldschool Runescape Economy? How The Summer Sweep Up Is Changing The Market What Is Happening To The Oldschool Runescape Economy? Did Jagex Kill The Bots? As soon as Jagex finds a consistent way to detect and ban a series of advanced bots, the clock starts running on the bot's developers coming up with methods of evasion. One case of "hard price" inflation in RuneScape, was when Jagex raised the store price of chaos and death runes to be close to the typical player trading price, as the low prices aided auto-buying bots who camped in the stores and bought all the stock as it respawned. Oct 10, 2025 · Over the course of this past summer and into September, Jagex has taken steps to address its self-described overbearing monetization problem by running what it calls “MTX experiments” in RuneScape. Remember when jagex hired real world economists to take a look at the game and give suggestions on things they could do to fix the economy? We got the GE tax and item sink system out of it and the economy has been better than ever before. The latest from Jagex and RuneScape: updates, releases, community news and press. Stay up to date with what’s happening across our worlds. How does the Grand exchange work in Old School RuneScape? With the advent of the Grand Exchange, players can save time (and bank space) by having the system sell their items while they leave to play the wider game. ^ "Old School Economy - Future Plans". Old School RuneScape News. Jagex. 4 November 2021. Archived from the original. What is the economy in RuneScape? The economy in RuneScape bears many similarities to economies in the real world. In RuneScape, items can be produced, exchanged and used by players. Players can exchange these items through trading or via the Grand Exchange (the market). Grand Exchange prices vary due to many factors, the most basic one being supply and demand. Does RuneScape have 'hard price' inflation? One case of "hard price" inflation in RuneScape, was when Jagex raised the store price of chaos and death runes to be close to the typical player trading price, as the low prices aided auto-buying bots who camped in the stores and bought all the stock as it respawned. Is releasing statistics a lose/lose for Jagex? Releasing statistics is lose/lose for Jagex. With people being able to compare numbers if they go up then its "dead game, bot epidemic, all these bans and still bots everywhere" and if they go down its "dead game, bot epidemic, they're not even bothering anymore" This isn’t the case.

Recent deterministic policy shifts have introduced a mild risk-off tilt via patch-window controls.
